reviews.quote: The Yoga Slim 7x isn't just an alternative in ways that matter day-to-day. It's actually better. Lighter, brighter screen with actual black instead of gray, double the refresh rate, more keyboard travel, touchscreen if you want it. Same performance unplugged.
The new Lenovo Slim 7X, it's an awesome device this year. Super fast chip, crazy battery life.

praises: Touchscreen 2.8K OLED option adds pen annotation without the 2-in-1 weight penalty (Rettinger: 'touchscreen if you want it')
2TB built-in suits travellers who can't carry drives
Still ~1.25kg with touch — lightest touch OLED 14-inch class
Battery still clears 13h light use despite touch layer
Max RAM/storage config stays relevant for 4-5 years of heavy use
complaints: Glossy touch glass reflects more than the non-touch tier
Touch adds ~$300 over the 32GB/1TB tier for a feature many don't use
No Thunderbolt/SD on the top config either
Integrated GPU remains the line's weak point for gaming and 3D

design_philosophy: The fully-optioned Slim 7x: Snapdragon X2 Elite with double storage and the PureSight Pro touch OLED, for creators who want pen input and maximum capacity in Lenovo's lightest premium 14-inch chassis.
rating_notes: Inferred from same-line X2 Elite anchor: touch tier → pen_touch 6.5, readability_bright −0.2 (gloss), battery −0.2; 2TB → creative_work +0.2 vs 1TB sibling. Same 32GB productivity as 26.json.
